PullRequest.Title: chat: add accessible previews for inline GitHub references
PullRequest.Body:

Adds GitHub issue and pull request detail previews to inline references in the Chat composer, so users can inspect the title, status, description, and branches without leaving or submitting their draft. Reuses the existing chat reference-card renderer and GitHub details resolver.

Related: #334061.

## Interaction

- Intentional pointer hover or pausing with a reference selected by arrow keys opens its preview after `workbench.hover.delay` (500 ms on Windows/Linux and 1500 ms on macOS by default). User overrides are respected; adjacent pointer previews share the hover service's group.
- Click or Enter opens the referenced item through the existing attachment navigation handlers. Inside the preview, the linked number also opens the item; branch buttons copy their names.
- Showing or resolving a preview never transfers focus automatically. Tab enters real links and copy controls once available. Escape, Shift+Tab from the first link, or Tab from the last control returns to the composer.
- Modified Tab shortcuts still reach the workbench. A locked keyboard preview stays available when the hover service rejects a pointer replacement; pending pointer previews cancel on leave even if the chip remains selected.
- Pointer-opened cards remain available while their controls have keyboard focus. They return to ordinary pointer behavior after focus leaves rather than becoming permanently sticky.
- Composer refreshes preserve the currently focused card and control. Deferred chip updates apply after the preview is dismissed, instead of closing and reopening it under the keyboard user.

## Shared fetching and accessibility

The input retains one resolver across chip rerenders, preserving the existing in-flight coalescing, freshness limits, cancellation, and account invalidation. Shared `retain()` prunes removed targets and warms new arrivals after the initial snapshot through the existing bounded prefetch path. No separate timer, cache, retry loop, polling, or loading/failure card is added.

A cold lookup can briefly display the shared plain-text reference label; an unavailable lookup uses the shared URL fallback. These states have no focusable placeholder. External reference surfaces that already fetched or prefetched metadata can display the resolved card immediately.

Resolved cards provide a named nonmodal preview. Accessible View presents details as text, and Accessibility Help explains navigation and returning to the draft. Opening Help, clicking the accessible editor or toolbar, loading completion, and composer rerenders preserve the preview's DOM ownership and return focus to the invoking control.

**High Contrast Dark:** the existing reference-opening link uses the theme's visible focus treatment. This retained image illustrates the unchanged resolved card, not the hover delay.

![Keyboard focus on the reference-opening link in High Contrast Dark](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/509dab27-7b42-475d-8d2a-606bb8d09e4a)

Native Windows delayed hover rendered real GitHub details; arrow selection, Tab entry, and Escape return were checked. Cache retention, adjacent-hover timing, focused-card lifetime, nested cancellation, and teardown are covered by the focused tests below. Earlier NVDA 2026.3 generated-utterance checks covered title/status/description, Open and Copy control names, Accessible View/help, and focus return; the latest trigger/cache/lifecycle changes weren't rechecked with NVDA. Audio playback and native screen readers on other operating systems weren't tested.

## How to test

1. Sign in to GitHub and turn on `chat.inlineAttachments.enabled`. Paste an accessible issue or pull request URL into an unsent Chat draft, such as https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/345729.
2. Hover the reference intentionally. It should wait for the configured delay, then show details without taking focus. Moving away before the delay should cancel it. A first uncached request may show the passive shared fallback before details arrive.
3. Move the caret past the reference with arrow keys and pause. Tab should enter the resolved preview's links and copy controls. Escape or either Tab boundary should return to the unchanged draft.
4. Click the chip, or select it with arrows and press Enter, to open the referenced item rather than submit the prompt.
5. With a resolved control focused, open Accessible View (Alt+F2 on Windows) and Help (Alt+F1). Read or select the editor/toolbar, close the view, and confirm focus returns to the invoking control.
6. Edit surrounding prompt text and reopen the preview within its freshness window. It should reuse cached details rather than refetch because a chip rerendered.

  ```powershell
  .\scripts\test.bat --reporter dot `
    --run src\vs\workbench\contrib\chat\test\browser\widget\input\editor\chatInlineAttachments.test.ts `
    --run src\vs\workbench\contrib\chat\test\browser\widget\chatContentParts\chatAttachmentsContentPart.test.ts `
    --run src\vs\workbench\contrib\github\test\browser\githubResourceDetails.test.ts `
  ```

The same selectors through `node test\unit\browser\index.js --browser chromium --browser webkit --reporter dot` — **385 passed in each browser**.

Coverage includes exact default/custom delay boundaries, cancellation, adjacent-hover grouping, real URI navigation, passive loading/failure, late-arriving controls without focus stealing, resolver reuse across widget recreation, account changes, and Accessible View/help ownership. Full integration and smoke suites weren't run locally.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The call chain from the changed synchronous getHoverContent call through CachedChatPillHover._render to concrete GitHub subscription.refresh operations is direct. The only magnitude uncertainty is how many cold references users traverse before the delay, not whether those requests start early.
Findings.PerformanceResource: GitHub client acquisitions and issue/PR refresh network requests (including PR checks)
Findings.PerformanceScaling: On a cold cache, each distinct reference crossed by the pointer or arrow keys starts one interactive resolution; rapidly traversing N references can therefore start N independent requests, and interactive resolutions bypass the resolver's three-request prefetch limiter.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Excess network traffic and request bursts, with avoidable authentication/client work and GitHub API pressure for previews that never become visible.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Inline GitHub pills had no detail-preview resolution path, so merely moving the pointer or cursor across them did not acquire a GitHub client or refresh issue/PR data.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: _showPillPreview calls getHoverContent synchronously before passing the resulting element to showDelayedHover. The content factory immediately renders CachedChatPillHover, whose cold render invokes resolver.resolveIssue/resolvePullRequest, while HoverService only waits for workbench.hover.delay after the hover widget has already been created.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: The added call at RIGHT line 1333 constructs/resolves preview content synchronously on pointer/keyboard activation, before the added showDelayedHover call later in the same method can enforce the configured delay.
Findings.Title: Defer GitHub resolution until the delayed preview is shown
Findings.Impact: With the default 500–1500 ms delay, a user can leave a cold reference before any card is shown yet still trigger its GitHub request. Arrowing or sweeping across several references can launch a burst of interactive API work even though all pending previews are cancelled visually.
Findings.Evidence: At the changed line, pill.getHoverContent() runs before showDelayedHover. DefaultChatAttachmentWidget.getPreviewHoverContent calls content(), and CachedChatPillHover._render starts provider.resolve whenever the cache is cold. That reaches GitHubResourceDetailsResolver._resolveIssue/_resolvePullRequest, which acquires the default account client and calls subscription.refresh; pull requests may also refresh checks. HoverService applies the configured delay only after _createHover returns, and clearing the hover does not abort these requests because retain() keeps every reference target cached.
Findings.Recommendation: Keep cold content creation side-effect free until onDidShow (or add a delayed-hover content factory that is evaluated only after the timer). Start/promote resolution only when the preview actually becomes visible, while preserving the existing resolver coalescing and bounded prefetch behavior.

Scenarios.Scenario: Cold inline GitHub reference preview opened or merely crossed by pointer/arrow navigation
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The changed activation path synchronously calls getHoverContent before HoverService begins its configured delay. CachedChatPillHover starts resolution immediately; visible preview progress later depends on GitHub client acquisition and issue/PR refresh, but cancelled-before-deadline previews should not have required that work.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Acquire the default GitHub account client and refresh issue details through a query subscription.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most once concurrently per distinct cold issue target; N distinct traversed issues can create N resolutions.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Inline GitHub pills did not resolve detail previews on pointer or cursor traversal.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Starts before the hover delay and therefore runs even when the preview never appears; when shown, completion supplies the resolved card.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Acquire the default GitHub account client, refresh pull-request core data, then refresh checks for interactive requests.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One core refresh and potentially one checks refresh per distinct cold PR target; N distinct traversed PRs can run concurrently.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Inline GitHub pills did not resolve PR details or checks on pointer or cursor traversal.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Starts before the hover delay and can perform both refresh stages even when the pending preview is cancelled visually.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of distinct cold GitHub issue/PR pills traversed before their 500–1500 ms delay expires; effective cardinality is one resolution per distinct target because the resolver coalesces duplicate targets.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Interactive resolutions are not sent through the three-request prefetch limiter, so distinct cold targets traversed rapidly can resolve concurrently without a shared aggregate bound; same-target requests coalesce.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Fresh issue/PR entries avoid network resolution. Cold entries start resolution immediately and remain retained while the reference stays in the composer, so visually cancelling a pending hover does not abort them. Duplicate targets share the resolver entry.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: Very high: the changed synchronous content call, cold-render resolution, delayed-hover timer placement, concrete refresh boundaries, and lack of cancellation on visual dismissal are directly traced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Most drafts contain few references and warm cache hits are cheap; the prevalence of users rapidly traversing many cold references is uncertain, which keeps severity medium.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable: the diff moves cold GitHub network work ahead of the intentional hover delay and permits avoidable request bursts for previews never shown.

Scenarios.Scenario: Composer reconciliation, rerender, and retention of GitHub reference cache
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Every model/cursor/attachment reconciliation reaches _renderPills. The diff scans pills and calls resolver.retain before the render fast-path; ordinary typing/cursor progress does not await this synchronous work. Newly retained targets may schedule background prefetch off the immediate critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Background prefetch issue or pull-request core details for targets newly added to the same retained scope.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One prefetch per distinct newly arrived target, globally limited to three active tasks for this resolver.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Inline attachment reconciliation did not retain or warm GitHub detail metadata.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Scheduled during reconciliation but performed asynchronously; not awaited by typing/render progress.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: All inline pills for the synchronous scan; distinct newly added GitHub targets for prefetch. Duplicate targets deduplicate in resolver sets/cache.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Background prefetch uses a Limiter of 3, so at most three prefetch executions are active even when several new targets arrive. Reconciliation itself is serialized/coalesced by one queued microtask.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: retain preserves current target caches, prunes removed targets, and distinguishes session scope. A new resolver/session snapshot is not prefetched; later arrivals in the same scope are warmed. Removed targets abort and delete their entries.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for the synchronous O(pills) scan and bounded prefetch mechanics; lower for material CPU impact, so no additional finding was submitted.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Large attachment collections make the new allocation/parsing scan more noticeable, but realistic cardinality and timing are insufficient to establish a separate user-visible CPU regression beyond existing collection-wide reconciliation.
Scenarios.Verdict: No separate finding: network prefetch is intentionally scoped, deduplicated, cancellable on removal, and concurrency-limited; the added synchronous scan lacks evidence of material impact at realistic collection sizes.

Scenarios.Scenario: Resolved preview keyboard focus, Accessible View, composer refresh, and teardown
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Showing and focusing the card creates DOM, focus trackers, hover listeners, and MutationObservers. Accessible View snapshots text and temporarily hides the same hover; composer rerenders are deferred while ownership/focus must remain stable. No subprocess, IPC, filesystem, database, or network boundary is newly reached solely by these lifecycle operations.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: One active preview per ChatInlineAttachments controller; DOM/text work scales with one resolved card's content and tabbable controls, not the full editor history.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Hover service serializes the active delayed hover/group. Accessible View uses one MutationObserver for the active card; composer reconciliation remains microtask-coalesced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The same resolver/hover content is reused while fresh. Account changes invalidate resolver weak caches and clear displayed preview content. Closing or replacing the preview disposes observers/listeners and applies any deferred rerender.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: ownership and disposal paths are explicit in MutableDisposable/DisposableStore cleanup and account-change handling.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Resolved descriptions vary in length, but only one card is observed/read at a time and no unbounded retained collection was found.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: DOM and observer lifetime is bounded to one active preview and cleanup covers dismissal, replacement, account invalidation, input disposal, and deferred rerender.

Scenarios.Scenario: General workbench hover behavior after focus/visibility tracking changes
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Hover creation now installs focus tracking on the hover container and dismissal checks visibility/focus. These are synchronous DOM/listener operations on hover creation and mouse/focus transitions; no external expensive boundary is reached.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: One tracker/listener set per live hover, bounded by the hover stack and maximum nesting depth; focus checks scan the small tracked-element array.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Hover creation/dismissal is service-serialized through the current hover stack; timers are individually disposed with their widgets.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for the added work and bounded lifecycle; insufficient evidence of material performance impact.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Hover frequency is high product-wide, but the added constant-size listeners and active-element checks do not establish measurable rendering/layout or CPU degradation from code evidence alone.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding: the additional work is constant and disposed with each hover, with no demonstrated forced layout, unbounded retention, or scaling boundary fan-out.

Analysis.Summary: Reviewed all 16 changed files and complete paginated patches for the performance focus. Traced inline preview activation through hover timing, shared resolver caching, GitHub client/query refreshes, bounded prefetch, composer reconciliation, Accessible View ownership, and hover cleanup. Submitted one medium-severity eager-network finding because cold resolution begins before the configured delay and survives visual cancellation; no other changed mechanism met the evidence threshold.
